title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This is page 18 of a typescript, with handwritten corrections. It looks like part of an 'errata et addenda' to EGA IV, chapter IV (references 6.14.1, 6.14.1.1, 6.14.4, 17.5.7). It is not related to the crystalline and de Rham material on the neighbouring pages; it was probably filed with them by accident.

The remark concerns the proof of EGA IV 6.14.4, a result on normality (geometric normality) of a ring B' obtained by base change, roughly B' = B ⊗_A C. The point is that this proof does not need the hard part of 6.14.1, the theorem on reducedness and normality of tensor products over a field.

1. The successive reductions in the proof of 6.14.4 bring one, without using 6.14.1, to the case where C is an integral domain and A is its fraction field.
2. In that case B is a normal ring, and Spec(B') → Spec(B) is étale.
3. A ring étale over a normal ring is normal (EGA IV 17.5.7), so B' is normal.
4. The argument then finishes using only the elementary lemma 6.14.1.1.

So the logical dependence of 6.14.4 on 6.14.1 is cut down to 6.14.1.1 plus the étale-descent fact 17.5.7. This is a remark about the structure of proofs; it contains no new theorem.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The page starts mid-sentence ('effet', i.e. '[En] effet'), so the exact statement of 6.14.4 being proved cannot be checked from this page alone.

ideas.what: Normality ascends along étale morphisms (a ring étale over a normal ring is normal), used to simplify the proof of the normality of base changes in EGA IV 6.14.4
ideas.modern_name: Étale (more generally smooth or regular-fibred) ascent of normality
ideas.where_published: EGA IV 17.5.7. The rerouting of the proof of 6.14.4 was most likely printed in the Errata et addenda of EGA IV (4e partie, 1967) – unsure of the exact location

ideas.what: Avoiding the difficult part of the proof of 6.14.1 (normality and reducedness of tensor products) by reducing to C integral with A = Frac(C)
ideas.modern_name: Proof-economy remark / erratum to EGA IV §6.14
ideas.where_published: Probably EGA IV4, Errata et addenda to IV2
